sprint: Image Studio Ship C — Bring It Back = Oops, ✂️ Scissors + Back Buttons + Circular Brush Sizes + BG Strength Slider. Direct product request (verbatim): 'bring it back is actually oops functionality. i would like bring it back button to work like oops button. remove oops button than. in every contextual panel where there is done button give one back button. for brushes instead of writing small medium large give circles of small medium large sizes. in trim functinality give scissors. for background remover also give slider to increase or decrease the transparency layer or background removing strength.' Five sub-tasks landed together in one ship, all in `js/pictureStudio.js`/`css/style.css`. (A) ❤️ Bring It Back rewired to call `_undoBrushStroke()` (the pre-existing per-stroke undo from Oops's own `_cleanupHistory` stack); ✋ Oops tile removed outright as now-genuinely-duplicated; the `'restore'` brush mode retired entirely (`_brushMode` now 'erase' | null only), documented in a code comment. (B) A new `← Back` button appended alongside every `✓ Done` button in the sub-panel actions row (`.picture-studio-edit-actions-row`, `display:none` by default, `display:flex` when any tool is active via `.picture-studio[data-active-tool='brush|crop|flip|reset']` per-tool CSS); both call `_toggleActiveTool(null)` and reset the active tool identically, but styled distinctly — Back is a paper-tone recessive appearance vs. Done's gold pill CTA — so the visual weight matches each action's own intent. (C) The three brush size buttons no longer render 'Small'/'Medium'/'Large' text; each now renders as a real circular dot at a real, size-proportional diameter — new `SIZE_VISUAL_PX={small:10,medium:16,large:24}` map applied via `dot.style.width/height`+`border-radius:50%`, so the dot itself previews the brush's own relative width. (D) A new floating `✂️` scissors cursor (`_scissorsCursor`, mirroring `_brushCursor`'s exact absolute-positioned-inside-`.picture-studio-stage` pattern) appears whenever crop mode is active, tracking the pointer live via the same `mousemove` handler chain — a genuine visual cue that the pointer is a cutting tool right now, not just a pointer. (E) A new 0-100 BG strength slider inside the brush sub-panel (labelled 'How strong?', shown only in brush mode) lets the Story Author push the background-removal worker's tolerance higher or lower — its 'change' event fires `_bgStrengthOverride=pct; _startBgRemoval();`, threading the override into `worker.postMessage({options:{tolerance:_bgStrengthOverride}})` at the one existing call site (`if(_bgStrengthOverride!=null) opts.tolerance=_bgStrengthOverride`). `_hide()` resets `_bgStrengthOverride=null` and returns the slider to 50 so a fresh session always starts at the worker's own default.
